page: Amazon Web Services x1.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for memory-intensive workloads. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor running at 2.3 GHz, delivering 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system is equipped with 1952.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.25 GB per physical core. It includes 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, running on the Xen hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core or memory-bound operations. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 10% according to stress-ng and Geekbench metrics, and single-threaded compression tasks are weak. However, the instance excels in memory bandwidth, with both read and write large-block operations scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and database operations reside in the average middle 50% tier. Static web serving throughput is strong, also placing in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x1.32xlarge offers high resource density for applications requiring massive memory footprints without needing top-tier single-core compute speeds. The bundled 3.8 TB NVMe SSD storage and high memory bandwidth make it highly suitable for large in-memory databases, enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks or high-performance text generation workloads, where its older CPU architecture and lower single-core speeds present performance bottlenecks.
